This scenario excludes the electoral college entirely. You actually don't need a popular election for the Electoral College to choose a President. The states can appoint their electors in the manner they see fit. Then

the electors meet "on the first Monday after the second Wednesday in December next following their appointment" to vote for president and vice president.

We're getting into bizarre contingencies here; likely the State Legislatures and EC could figure out a new POTUS for us even with COVID - no need for polling places or mail in voting.

If the Electors don't transmit a winner with an absolute majority, then the (new) House of Representatives will be forced to choose from the top three vote-winners that the Electors sent. The (new) Senate would choose from the top two vote-winners for Vice President if no candidate had a majority.

IF however, a new House was not elected on time, the terms would expire (on Jan. 3), and the House would be vacant until such time as a special election could be held (individual states figure this out on their own, and may send the Congressional delegations slowly but surely). In the meantime, the remaining Senate can resolve the failed Electoral College with their choice for VP. Remember also that most states provide for emergency appointments to the Senate if the General Election didn't occur.

At that point, the Senate's VP choice will be acting President UNTIL a Special Election is called and the New House of Representatives selects the President.

Now, you'd think at this point that if Pelosi retains her speakership in the new Congress that it's a foregone conclusion that they would elect a Democrat. Not necessarily

Each state delegation votes en bloc, with each state having a single vote. A candidate is required to receive an absolute majority of state delegation votes (currently 26 votes) in order for that candidate to become the president-elect. The District of Columbia, which is not a state, does not receive a vote. The House continues balloting until it elects a president..
